In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of ecdysoid biosynthesis in D. melanogastor, and with the woc gene and its product.

the identification and characterization of a novel gene (woc) that encodes an essential component of the 7-dehydrogenation pathway of cholesterol, the first and rate limiting step in ecdysone synthesis.
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the regulation of ecdysoid biosynthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
woc controls 7,8- dehydrogenase activity in D. melanogaserster ring glands, which in turn controls ecdysone production.
the woc mutation causes a block in the 7, 8-dehydrogenating step of ecdysoid biosynthesis, which is the first step in ecydsoidogenesis.
the Woc gene product is a negative regulator that controls the first step of ecdysteroid biosynthesis, and that this control is exerted at the level of the 7-dehydrogenase enzyme activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the woc mutation blocks the first committed step in ecdysone synthesis, i.e. 7,8- dehydrogenation of C to 7d25-C.

the woc mutant phenotype results from the absence of 7,8-sterol dehydrogenase activity in vivo, and the absence of 25-hydroxylated 7,8-stereoids in the ring gland, the source of ecdysoids in larvae and adults.
woc mutants lack a functional 7,8-Delta(5,7) sterol isomerase, and that this enzyme plays a critical role in ecdysteroneogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of the Woc gene product, the Delta(5,8)-7-dehydrogenase is inactive and the Delta(7)-7-dehydrocholesteryl ester is the major endogenous substrate for E biosynthesis in D. melanogastor.
the woc mutation blocks ecdysone production in vivo by preventing the first step in the ecdysteroidogenic pathway, i.e. 7,8-dihydrogenation.
the woc mutation blocks the first step in eedysteroidogenesis, and this is the reason why homozygous mutants do not pupate.
